name: Biology PhD — Cell and Molecular Biology
summary: Biology PhD with a Cell and Molecular Biology concentration at Toledo. Applicants need a faculty member who will work with them. Doctoral students receive tuition waivers and stipends for teaching or research work.
detailsNote: The department has no fixed application deadline: it says it admits on a rolling basis, with applications accepted all year for Fall, Spring and Summer starts. GRE and the number of recommendation letters are not stated on the program pages, so they are left out. The fee and English scores come from University of Toledo graduate-wide pages, not the department. The fee statement comes from the catalog admission PDF and the College of Engineering FAQ.

english.note: University-wide minimums for applicants whose native language is not English and who earned their undergraduate degree at a non-English-speaking institution. Scores must be sent by the testing service and still valid on the first day of the program. A foreign credential evaluation is required for all applicants.

applicationFee.note: The graduate fee is $45 for domestic applicants and $75 for international applicants. The pages checked do not mention fee waivers.

documents: Transcripts from all previous higher education institutions
Online application (University of Toledo College of Graduate Studies)
requirements.note: The graduate catalog says some programs have additional requirements and that letters of recommendation depend on the program; the program's own count is not stated on the pages checked. Applicants must be approved by a faculty member who will work with them; contacting faculty directly is encouraged.

funding.note: The program page says all doctoral students receive tuition waivers and competitive stipends, in return for work as a teaching or research assistant. It does not say whether this covers international students. The department says support usually comes through the major professor's grant. No stipend amount is stated.
